title: Meet-in-the-Middle Compilation of the $[\mathrm{CNOT}]$ Class with Fibonacci Anyons
abstract: Compilation of two-qubit Fibonacci anyon gates is complicated by leakage ($\ell$) from the four-dimensional computational sector to the fifth state of the fusion space. We construct a GPU pipeline to find low-leakage representatives of the $[\text{CNOT}]$ class on different subsets of the braid group. We exhaustively explore the full positive five-generator alphabet up to $L=21$ with minimal leakage $\ell\sim10^{-3}$ and error $d_{[\text{CNOT}]}\sim 10^{-8}$ on it. To reach larger lengths, the search space is successively narrowed to three-generator, boundary-$σ_3$, and palindromic braids, and by considering only the Garside left normal form. These optimizations allow us to reach $L=72$. For $L=69$, a braid with $\ell\sim10^{-10}$ and $d_{[\text{CNOT}]}\sim 10^{-10}$ is found. In addition to directly enumerating optimal braids, we proved that $\ell\in\mathbb Z[\varphi]$, and any nonzero leakage obeys an exponential lower bound in the braid length, and obtained the limit laws $F_{3,\infty}(\ell)=\ell^2$ and $F_{5,\infty}(\ell)=\ell^4$ for our sets. Using asymptotics for the distribution function $F$, we showed that for sufficiently long braids, the asymptotics of exhaustive search are better than the asymptotics of random sampling for finding low-leakage braids.

bite.hook: Found a braid of length 69 with leakage and error around 10^-10 for compiling CNOT gates with Fibonacci anyons.
tldr: Built a GPU pipeline to find low-leakage representatives of the CNOT gate class using Fibonacci anyons.
Exhaustively explored braid alphabets up to length 21 and optimized search spaces using palindromic braids and Garside normal forms up to length 72.
Proved leakage obeys an exponential lower bound in braid length and derived limit laws showing exhaustive search beats random sampling.
bite.whyItMatters: Fibonacci anyons are a promising route to fault-tolerant quantum computing, but compiling precise quantum gates without leaking information is notoriously difficult. This work provides concrete pathways and computational pipelines to make those gates reliable.
bite.eli5: Weaving quantum gates with exotic particles called anyons is a bit like braiding hair: if you slip up, information leaks out and ruins the calculation. Scientists built a powerful computer program to find the absolute best ways to braid these particles without making mistakes.
